title: Authoring
description: Writing a product down in Lathe's one language, as typed data: the fifty kinds from products and domains to tests, each record with one parent, the links between them, the kinds and relations a product declares as its own, and changing all of it through the command layer. The schema is the language, and the reference shows it whole.
notes: The checks that hold records to these rules are designed here, beside the rules; Checking runs them and reports what they find.

title: Checking
description: Running the checks and reporting what they find: each check is a row of the `check` table with its query, a problem names its check and its record, and an error means the data is broken while a warning is work still to do. What the schema enforces never reaches a check: the store refuses it, and data it refuses is one `data-refused` error per refusal. A product adds check rows of its own. Checking also keeps the checks the schema cannot hold: records that nothing uses, the shape warnings (a test at a level its kind does not allow, a command's recorded exception, an event not delivered by outbox), and levels of the spec that are the wrong size. Every problem shows on the Checks page and the Dock badge.

title: Exploring
description: Reading a product: its pages at their addresses, the wiki, Graph, ERD and Trace views side by side, the nav and its stage folders, quick find, spaces, tabs and the side bar's content. The pages read the product's data, and a record's page also changes it: an edit, a new child or a removal goes through the command layer, as an Agent's writes do, and every change lands in the data files for review in git.

title: Platform
description: What every slice stands on: the app shell and workbench with its panels, commands and keys, themes, the workspace loaded from the data files and reloaded live, the command layer every write goes through, the server and its API's transport, and the desktop app, a window per product folder around the same web app. Platform follows the two app patterns, App code (`LA-PAT-APP-CODE`) and App experience (`LA-PAT-APP-UX`), and holds the standards, stability, accessibility and performance suites that prove them for the whole app.
notes: The desktop app runs three ways: `npm --prefix desktop run dev` for development, which loads the owner's dev server on port 5199 when it serves the opened folder or else one of its own; `npm --prefix desktop start`, which builds Lathe and runs the shell as it ships; and `npm --prefix desktop run pack`, an unsigned macOS app for this Mac. Signed builds, notarizing, auto-update and Windows and Linux builds come later and need the owner's approval to publish.

title: Traceability
description: Following what designs, builds and proves each obligation, and counting it: coverage per domain and obligation kind, designed through flow steps and the technical records that implement each design, built through their files and proved through the tests under each obligation; the gaps, each domain's tests by state, the pattern rules each domain owes, and each record's traceability. The engine counts it, and the app shows it on the product and domain pages and in each record's Traceability section.
